name: Ferr

modes.label: Cloud browser overage unpublished
modes.note: Unspecified guest OS is not a selectable OS guarantee.

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: Live page, unchanged: '$99 / month ... 1,000 browser hours included ... 50 concurrent sessions ... Stealth mode & profiles ... Dedicated IP add-ons'. Overage rate is not published. Blog 2026-06-12: plans 'bill on browser hours — the time your sessions are actually open'.

plans.name: Scale
plans.note: Custom volume rate; unlimited concurrency advertised; SLA/self-hosting option.

features.ip_note: Residential or dedicated addresses per project; stealth mode and dedicated IP add-ons listed on Pro ($99/mo); no per-GB price published.

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv 4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.

No guaranteed vCPU allocation published; browser-hour is not a verified 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM equivalent. The sizes card keeps unknown hardware null; do not coerce it to zero or auto-rank against resource-guaranteed VMs.
Browser RAM is not published unless a specific mode overrides it.
Official landing provides pricing/features, but docs.ferr.dev failed DNS and /docs returned 404. These marketing claims were not independently provisioned.
Open-source and self-host options are advertised; no evidence of zero managed overage. Hourly rate stays null rather than extrapolating $99/1000.

ferr.dev appears to be a clone or rebrand of Steel.dev's marketing site (ferrum = iron, i.e. 'steel'): Steel's blog slugs appear with 'steel' changed to 'ferr', and the author personas are generic. The product endpoints (docs, app, GitHub, PyPI, Docker) don't exist. Treat it as non-existent until a signup works.

fleet.tiers: Hobby 3; Pro 50; Scale advertised unlimited via sales.
fleet.notes: Browser-session quota; 10/50 require Pro, 300/1,000 negotiated. Unlimited is not a fleet reservation.

status: unverifiable: marketing page only; exclude from default ranking

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

image_oci.quote: Ferr is an open-source browser API that lets you control fleets of browsers in the cloud.
image_oci.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Ferr launches managed Chrome browser sessions via an API, not arbitrary machines booted from a customer OCI/Docker image.

docker_inside.quote: Ferr is an open-source browser API that lets you control fleets of browsers in the cloud.
docker_inside.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — sessions are single Chrome browser instances, not general compute where you'd run nested containers.

nested_virt.quote: Ferr is an open-source browser API that lets you control fleets of browsers in the cloud.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no /dev/kvm or VM-in-VM capability is offered on a browser-session product.

desktop.quote: Every session ships with a live view, full network logs, and a replay you can scrub to see exactly what happened.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — sessions expose a browser live-view/replay, not a general graphical desktop (VNC/RDP) of an OS.

ssh.quote: launch a cloud browser ... await ferr.sessions.create({ stealth: true })
ssh.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — access is via CDP/Playwright/Puppeteer to a browser session, not SSH to a machine.

snapshot.quote: Save cookies, local storage, and auth state to a profile and reuse it across sessions to stay logged in.
snapshot.note: Browser Profiles persist auth/cookie state across sessions, but there is no mention of filesystem or memory snapshotting of a running session/process.

snapshot_auto.quote: Save cookies, local storage, and auth state to a profile and reuse it across sessions to stay logged in.
snapshot_auto.note: not offered: only profile-based cookie/storage persistence is described, not an automatic full session snapshot/restore.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Save cookies, local storage, and auth state to a profile and reuse it across sessions to stay logged in.
snapshot_on_demand.note: not offered: no API/CLI snapshot or checkpoint mechanism is described; only saved profiles (cookies/local storage).

fork.quote: Ferr is an open-source browser API that lets you control fleets of browsers in the cloud.
fork.note: not offered: no clone/fork-a-machine feature is described anywhere on the site.

fork_running.quote: Ferr is an open-source browser API that lets you control fleets of browsers in the cloud.
fork_running.note: not offered: no fork feature at all, let alone forking a running session.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Ferr is an open-source browser API that lets you control fleets of browsers in the cloud.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: no fork/snapshot feature described.

pause_resume.quote: Spin up disposable browsers for end-to-end tests and visual checks, then tear them down the moment you are done.
pause_resume.note: not offered: sessions are described as created and torn down, not paused/resumed with reduced billing.

wake_on_request.quote: launch a browser in one call Create a session, get a live browser in the cloud
wake_on_request.note: not offered: sessions are explicitly created via an API call on demand; there is no described 'sleeping session' that wakes automatically on an inbound request.

persistent_disk.quote: Save cookies, local storage, and auth state to a profile and reuse it across sessions to stay logged in. Durable auth state. Reusable across runs.
persistent_disk.note: Browser Profiles persist cookies/local-storage/auth state across session stop/start, functioning like persistent storage for the browser's own state.

volume_attach.quote: Ferr is an open-source browser API that lets you control fleets of browsers in the cloud.
volume_attach.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no extra attachable block/file volumes are described; only browser profile storage.

volume_shared.quote: Ferr is an open-source browser API that lets you control fleets of browsers in the cloud.
volume_shared.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no shared-volume-across-machines concept exists for a browser-session product.

live_resize.quote: Ferr is an open-source browser API that lets you control fleets of browsers in the cloud.
live_resize.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — browser sessions have no described CPU/RAM sizing to resize; only concurrency/hour limits differ by plan.

agent_harnesses.quote: Ferr is an open-source browser API that lets you control fleets of browsers in the cloud.
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Ferr provides browser sessions for agents to drive, not preinstalled coding-agent harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, etc.).

harness_api.quote: Ferr is an open-source browser API that lets you control fleets of browsers in the cloud.
harness_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no first-party API to drive a coding agent harness is described.

own_agent_api.quote: Pair Ferr with your model of choice for reliable extraction.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: Ferr explicitly pairs with the customer's own AI/model (e.g. OpenAI) for extraction; it does not ship its own first-party research/browser task agent product.

lang_python.quote: First-class SDKs for Python and Node, with Rust and Go for systems teams — all wrapping one Sessions API.

lang_node.quote: First-class SDKs for Python and Node, with Rust and Go for systems teams — all wrapping one Sessions API.

public_ipv4.quote: Ferr is an open-source browser API that lets you control fleets of browsers in the cloud.
public_ipv4.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — there is no customer-addressable machine with inbound ports; sessions are outbound browser instances you drive via API/CDP.

inbound_https.quote: Ferr is an open-source browser API that lets you control fleets of browsers in the cloud.
inbound_https.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no inbound HTTPS URL to a customer service running in the session is described.

ingress_rules.quote: Ferr is an open-source browser API that lets you control fleets of browsers in the cloud.
ingress_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no exposed inbound ports exist to control access to.

egress_http_rules.quote: Ferr is an open-source browser API that lets you control fleets of browsers in the cloud.
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: no method/path-level egress rule feature is described anywhere on the site.

guest_firewall.quote: Ferr is an open-source browser API that lets you control fleets of browsers in the cloud.
guest_firewall.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — sessions are managed browser instances, not a root-accessible VM/microVM where the customer could configure nftables/iptables.

secret_proxy.quote: Save cookies, local storage, and auth state to a profile and reuse it across sessions to stay logged in.
secret_proxy.note: No first-party HTTP credential-injection proxy is described; auth is handled via saved browser profiles (cookies/local storage), not a secret-injecting API proxy.

static_egress_ip.quote: Dedicated IPs — Route traffic through residential or dedicated addresses per project to keep long-running jobs stable. ... Dedicated IP add-ons
static_egress_ip.note: Pro plan lists 'Dedicated IP add-ons' and the platform section describes routing sessions through dedicated addresses per project, i.e. a fixed outbound IP.

gpu.quote: Ferr is an open-source browser API that lets you control fleets of browsers in the cloud.
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Ferr is a headless-browser-session product, not a GPU compute provider; no GPU machines are advertised.

windows.quote: Ferr is an open-source browser API that lets you control fleets of browsers in the cloud.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no guest OS choice is offered; the product is a managed cloud browser (Chrome), not a Windows machine.

macos.quote: Ferr is an open-source browser API that lets you control fleets of browsers in the cloud.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no macOS machines are offered; the product is a managed cloud browser.

self_host.quote: Ferr Browser is open source, and self-hosting it is a container away. ... docker run -p 3000:3000 ferr/browser

byoc.quote: Ferr Browser is open source, and self-hosting it is a container away. ... You keep the API surface and trade managed capacity for full control.
byoc.note: not offered: what's described is customer-operated self-hosting (you run and manage the container yourself), not a provider-managed deployment into the customer's own cloud account.

open_source.quote: Ferr is an open-source browser API that lets you control fleets of browsers in the cloud.
open_source.note: License name is not stated on the pages read (GitHub org page did not expose repo/license details); marketing consistently calls it open source with '4.3k stars' and a public docker image.

isolation.note: Ferr Browser ships and runs as a Docker container image; the cloud product is described as running 'the same browser that powers our cloud' via containers, implying shared-kernel container isolation rather than a VM/microVM boundary. No dedicated hypervisor/VM isolation is documented.

captcha_solving.quote: Managed fingerprints Automatic header hygiene CAPTCHA-aware flows
captcha_solving.note: The site advertises Stealth Mode as 'CAPTCHA-aware', i.e. avoidance/fingerprinting to reduce CAPTCHA triggers, not an actual CAPTCHA-solving service. No CAPTCHA-solving API/feature is documented.

auto_stop_idle.quote: A browser that nobody is driving is just a meter running. Inactivity timeouts close a session automatically when it goes quiet, so a crashed agent never leaves a browser open for hours.
auto_stop_idle.note: Feature list on the same page: 'Close after a configurable idle period', 'Protect against runaway costs', 'Override per session when you need a long-lived browser'.

arm64.quote: Ferr is an open-source browser API that lets you control fleets of browsers in the cloud.
arm64.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Ferr sells managed Chrome browser sessions via an API/SDK; there is no customer-selectable machine or CPU architecture (no VM/instance sizing is exposed at all).
